description: Ordered verification gates. Run in order; stop at the first failure. A gate activates with the feature that makes it meaningful — never earlier (a gate that cannot fail teaches nothing) and never later (a gate added after the fact finds a backlog instead of a regression). Gates 1-4 and 6 went active with F-001, after being executed and seen to pass; they were deliberately NOT activated while pnpm install was blocked, because a gate that has never run is theatre. `ciStep: false` means the gate is deliberately covered inside another CI step; the ci-mirror check in verify-state.mjs knows that is intentional.

gates.description: Harness integrity. Validates feature_list.json and effects.json against their schemas; every E-### has a memory note and every memory note is referenced; every effect `to` path exists on disk; every critical link names a guard; wikilinks resolve; wip_limit is respected; blockers are done before a feature is in_progress; an in-flight feature has a plan; every PRD FR/NFR is claimed by a feature and appears in REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md; the ADR index matches the ADR files; gates.json mirrors the CI workflow; every IRODORA_* variable read by config is documented in .env.example; scoped rules do not weaken a golden rule; governed-doc relative links resolve.

TypeScript strict typecheck across the workspace. Runs each package's tsconfig.json — the same project the editor and typescript-eslint use — so tests are covered. tsconfig.build.json is the EMIT project only; running the build project here would leave type errors accumulating in files no gate can see.

ESLint 10 flat config, TYPE-AWARE via typescript-eslint against a real TypeScript program (TS 6.0.3 — ADR-0035). Enforces package boundaries, the colour engine platform-freedom rules, no-floating-promises, and later: no colour literals outside the token layer, no hard-coded user-facing strings, the claims copy lint. ALSO RUNS scripts/verify-guards.mjs, which writes a deliberately violating file at the exact path each rule targets and asserts the rule fires — ten boundaries, proven rather than assumed. A rule nobody has watched fail is not a boundary. NOTE: a later flat-config object REPLACES no-restricted-imports rather than merging, so the workspace patterns are repeated in the colour-engine override; guard #3 exists because that defect shipped once already.

Prettier formatting check on code and root config. Prose (docs/, .harness/) and byte-significant data (golden datasets, corpus JSON) are excluded — reflowing them makes review diffs unreadable and, for golden data, changes bytes that are compared by hash.

Unit, integration and property-based tests (Vitest + fast-check), including every port's adapter conformance suite. Each conformance suite contains at least one case verified to fail against a deliberately broken adapter — a conformance case that cannot fail launders every adapter through it.

The colour engine against published reference datasets. As of F-006: six cited datasets — the sRGB transfer function (IEC 61966-2-1) weighted at near-black, sRGB and Display-P3 primaries and matrices (CSS Color 4 / SMPTE RP 431-2), CIELAB's exact rationals (CIE 15:2018), Ottosson's published OKLab table, and Lindbloom's Bradford adaptation matrix — plus the cross-platform identity fixture: 10,000 seeded samples × 30 values, digested over IEEE-754 bytes and asserted bit-identical (NFR-3). Every entry declares whether it is a published value, computed from a published formula, or definitional, and an entry citing no source fails the load. F-007 added four more datasets in @irodora/color-difference: all 34 Sharma–Wu–Dalal CIEDE2000 pairs to four decimal places (each ALSO computed independently by culori, so a transcription error in the reference data is caught separately from an implementation error), WCAG contrast against its worked examples with every constant pinned digit-for-digit, APCA 0.0.98G-4g asserted BITWISE against colorjs.io, and a second determinism digest over the metrics — which is where a cross-engine divergence would appear first, since CIEDE2000 alone calls atan2, exp, sin, cos and pow. CVD confusion-line pairs join with F-008. Activated after being executed AND after each dataset was watched reject a real mutation: a pure-power transfer function, a column-swapped matrix (which leaves white BIT-identical), decimal-rounded ε and κ, and a 2% perturbation of any OKLab matrix element. A changed golden value requires an ADR — it is a claim about physical reality. The identity digest is a determinism fixture rather than such a claim, and regenerating it to make a test green is the one thing it exists to prevent.
Turborepo build of every package and app.

End-to-end per surface. API runs HTTP-surface e2e via app.inject. Web runs Playwright against its own server, including axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA assertions, a keyboard-only journey, a simulated-CVD journey, and a NETWORK assertion proving that a Lens scan transmits no image bytes (NFR-12). Tenancy negative tests run with a populated decoy tenant — against an empty one they pass whether or not the policy works.

Accessibility (axe, WCAG 2.2 AA) for every web route — zero violations, not warnings. Asserted inside the web Playwright run, so CI's e2e step covers it; ciStep is false deliberately and the ci-mirror check knows that. Listed separately for traceability against NFR-8.

Reads docs/design/design-system.manifest.json and asserts, in BOTH themes: every declared `pairsWith` combination meets the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum its `usage` selects, with APCA Lc reported alongside and never substituted (ADR-0021); every `srgb` value matches what the engine derives from that token OKLCh (ADR-0043); the chroma ceiling, with every exception recorded in the manifest rather than carved into the checker; and the structural rules carrying NFR-9. A pairing used in a component but absent from `pairsWith` is a failure — the declaration is how the gate knows what to check. Report-only while the manifest status is `placeholder`, blocking once it is `approved`; that switch is read from the manifest, not hard-coded. The arithmetic is NOT in the gate script: checkContrast/checkChromaCeiling/checkStructure live in @irodora/design-tokens so the gate and the tests run the same code, and every colour number under them comes from @irodora/color-difference. Translucent tokens are composited in LINEAR light over EVERY ground they declare, and judged on the worst — naming one favourable ground is how a check passes a border that is invisible where it is used. ACTIVATED after being watched fail on five real defects in the approved manifest, and after scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs asserted nine cases WITH the baseline green in each — six red: a token nudged below AA, a hand-edited hex, a removed chroma exception, a collapsed cvdPair, the status icon channel made optional (typecheck), and an emitter changed without regenerating; plus ONE that must stay green — a placeholder manifest status with a real failure present, which proves the report-only switch works in the direction that would otherwise look exactly like a passing build. THE COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE CHECKS: translucent tokens are now evaluated under BOTH the linear-light and the encoded compositing model and judged on the worse, because neither is uniformly stricter and the encoded one is what a browser actually draws; the CVD half evaluates ALL ELEVEN tabulated Machado severities rather than only 1.0, because Machado is not monotone in severity; it also evaluates Vienot total dichromacy for protan and deutan, because color-engine.md assigns total dichromacy to Vienot and the two models disagree by up to 5.6 points; and a token that no declared pairing covers is now a FAILURE unless it carries an `uncheckedReason`, because gate scope is driven by pairsWith and an unchecked token was previously indistinguishable from a passing one. The first cvdPair decoy did NOT discriminate — it was written against earlier token values and stopped collapsing the pair once status.warn moved, passing with the mutation applied; it was replaced with a 48-degree hue rotation that takes the pair from 64.1 to 31.8. THE RE-MEASUREMENT WAS ITSELF STALE for a while — the prose said 65.2 to 30.0 after the values moved again, which is the same defect one level up, and it was caught by the F-003 evaluation rather than by anything automatic. NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE: the half of this charter that scans RENDERED surfaces for colour-only status indicators. No component exists until F-017, and the gate says so on every run rather than implying coverage by being green. THE F-003 EVALUATION FOUND THE PROOF HAD A HOLE: no mutation isolated checkContrast, because the one contrast mutation also broke the ADR-0043 derived-hex check — so a checkContrast returning passes:true unconditionally left gate 9 exiting 0 and every other mutation green. Verified by neutering it. Case 8 now mutates the comparison itself and checks the PACKAGE TESTS rather than gate 9, because gate 9 alone genuinely does not catch it; test/check.test.ts covers the same ground with an independently recomputed ratio.

Colour-vision-deficiency regression, and the accessibility promise (NFR-10). Split from gate 5 deliberately: gate 5 asks whether the models reproduce their published values; this asks whether a pairing the product would recommend stays distinguishable — and that must be able to go red on its own. As of F-008 it covers the separation score shape: bounds, exact-zero identity, symmetry, severity clamping, severity-0 equivalence across deficiencies, monotonic degradation of a red-green pair, and the false negative the lightness term exists to avoid. ACTIVATED after being watched fail — deleting the lightness term from separation.ts makes it exit 1, restoring it exits 0. The FIRST version of that decoy did not discriminate: it used a pair where both terms saturate, and the gate passed with the term deleted. It was replaced with a pair where the term contributes 14.6 points, and the binding frequency (~9% of sampled pairs) is asserted so the case is not hand-picked. The design system cvdPairs assertion joins with F-003.

Corpus integrity (NFR-20). Fails the build if ANY entry lacks source, sourceType, derivation, verifiedBy or verifiedAt; if author and reviewer are the same identity; if a `historical` classification has no dated primary source; if a derived value is inconsistent with its xyz under the current engine; if a palette has no anchor; if a relation points at a missing slug; if a published entry differs from its checksum; or if a slug is duplicated. There is no partial publication — a corpus that is 95% verified is one where nobody knows which 5% to distrust.

Backend performance against ABSOLUTE committed thresholds (NFR-4), never baseline deltas — CI hardware varies, and a delta gate flakes until someone disables it. Boots the real Local runtime over a versioned deterministic corpus. Asserts recommendation p95 ≤ 200 ms, API p95 ≤ 300 ms, local analysis p95 ≤ 200 ms, capsule solve (40 garments) p95 ≤ 3 s. A miss is a tracked work item, never an edited threshold.

Frontend budgets (NFR-5). First-load JS per route, measured over the wire and gzipped, captured at the `load` event so lazily-imported chunks are correctly excluded — that exclusion IS the definition of the budget. Core Web Vitals measured by PerformanceObserver under prefers-reduced-motion with CPU throttling, median of 3 runs: LCP ≤ 2.0 s, CLS ≤ 0.05, TBT reported. Not Lighthouse: with animation running, TBT scales with the observation window rather than with the page. The honest limit: this does not measure what a motion-enabled visitor experiences. Requires the build gate to have run first.

Full-stack end-to-end against ONE live deployment — real API, real Postgres, real object storage, the production web build proxied at the live API. Runs the human journeys (J1 first value, J4 CVD check, J5 wardrobe) and the offline-to-online sync journey. Serialized with zero retries: a flaky full-stack gate is a lie, because it reports a state of the world it did not observe.

Secret scanning (gitleaks 8.30.1, pinned) and dependency audit. A Critical or High advisory blocks release (`pnpm audit --audit-level high`). A gitleaks finding ROTATES the secret — it never earns an allowlist entry, because a secret in git history is compromised regardless of whether the commit was pushed. CI installs the pinned binary and invokes THIS command rather than using gitleaks-action, so a workstation scan and a CI scan are the same scan. Activated after being executed (7 commits, no leaks) AND after its ruleset was watched fire on planted secrets outside git history — 3 of 4 shapes detected, exit 1. Note that gitleaks' default rules deliberately allowlist published example credentials such as AWS's AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE; a scan that stays green on those is correct, not broken.
